Convivial

kuhn-VIV-ee-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Convivial is friendly, lively, and enjoyable, especially in a social setting.

The tiny bakery's Sunday morning crowd had a convivial buzz, regulars trading sections of the newspaper across the communal table.

Worked Example

Even the awkward icebreaker games couldn't dampen the convivial mood of the retreat, as coworkers who'd never spoken before ended the night trading phone numbers.

Convivial describes a shared social warmth -- the specific, festive friendliness of a group enjoying each other's company.

How Convivial Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

festive

festive: cheerful and suited to a celebration

jovial

jovial: cheerful and friendly

Antonyms

somber

somber: dark, serious, and gloomy

unsociable

unsociable: not enjoying the company of others

How Strong Is It? — polite → convivial → riotous

polite vs. convivial

polite vs. convivial: Polite simply means well-mannered, without necessarily the warm, shared festivity of a convivial gathering.

riotous vs. convivial

riotous vs. convivial: Riotous goes even further than convivial, describing a gathering so lively and unrestrained it borders on chaos.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of convivial.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: with, together (Latin)

root — viv-

root — viv-: to live (Latin vivere)

suffix — -ial

suffix — -ial: relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Convivial comes from Latin con- ('with') plus vivere ('to live') and -ial ('relating to') -- literally 'relating to living together,' as people do when sharing a lively feast.

Use the root in a new word: revive

Use the root in a new word: revive: A splash of cold water helped revive the exhausted hikers.

Root Check

Word Choice

Convivial describes a shared, festive atmosphere -- notice that this unit also teaches Vivacious, from the very same viv- root. Vivacious describes one lively person's personality, while convivial describes a whole room's warm, social energy.
